audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags the chart as contradicting the data — Wukong wins 55.48% but Cassiopeia held five of seven stages — and three rows also contradicted their own whys[] line (win[0] and win[1] said Cassiopeia where the whys say 'even skill lane'; win[6] said Cassiopeia where the why says your Cyclone dive out-values her).
audit.why: Cassiopeia is a lane bully who loses the sidelane: she has no dash and no escape, so once Wukong has items Cyclone simply reaches her. Early is genuinely even before her poison ramps. The packet levelChart (Skill / Skill / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Wukong) matches the prose and closes most of the gap the defect names.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 3, 5 and 6 flipped in BOTH layers as matched pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown appeared on the page, so 'engage when Miasma is down' had no window attached to it.
audit.why: Miasma is 24/22/20/18/16s — a long, countable window and the single most important number in the lane. Noxious Blast is 3.5s flat and Twin Fang is 0.75s, which is why the mid-game trades are unwinnable rather than merely bad; Petrifying Gaze is 120/100/80s.
audit.corrected: 24s Miasma into phases[2].why and phases[5].why; the 3.5s and 0.75s cycle into phases[3].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: The grounding was stated generically as shutting off 'your E dash', and the build advice said to itemize armour.
audit.why: Miasma grounds, and Wukong has TWO movement abilities — Nimbus Strike and Warrior Trickster — so standing in the pool removes his engage and his escape at once, not just the gap-close. Cassiopeia deals magic damage, so armour is the wrong stat; the same entry already correctly recommends Mercury's Treads.
audit.corrected: Both movement abilities named in phases[2].why; armour swapped to magic resist in late, spikes[3].text and wants.you[2].
sources: champ-data/_kits/cassiopeia.json (W: 'Grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities')

notes: The mechanical content here was among the better entries in the slice — the grounding, the facing requirement on Petrifying Gaze and the flank advice were all correct. The defects were the chart (packet flagged it, and three rows fought their own whys), the missing cooldowns, and the armour recommendation against a pure magic-damage champion sitting next to a correct Mercury's Treads line.
